observations.overview: SSAB describes a strong North American plate market in Q3 2026, alongside rising prices.
observations.pricing: SSAB reports that North American plate prices increased during Q3 2026. This describes a quarterly trend, not a current spot quote or a price for a particular grade or size.
observations.demand: SSAB describes the North American plate market as strong in Q3 2026. Its commentary does not quantify present demand by consuming industry.
observations.domestic: SSAB assesses North American distributor inventories as somewhat low for the reported quarter. This is an inventory assessment, not a published mill allocation or delivery schedule.

quarters.label: Q4 2026
quarters.analysis: The base case for Q4 2026 is firming, with tightness risk. The remaining part of the current quarter carries the strongest link to the dated producer inventory and pricing evidence. Year-end inventory reduction could restrain demand, while constrained supply could limit price relief.
quarters.confidence_reason: Qualitative evidence strength, not a probability. Confidence declines with distance and missing plate-specific allocation, lead-time and transaction data.

scenarios.name: Bullish
scenarios.analysis: Longer plate lead times, an extended outage, tighter trade restrictions or executed energy, infrastructure and power-equipment orders would strengthen prices. Data-center spending matters only where it creates actual plate fabrication orders.

drivers.name: Mill production, allocations & shutdowns
drivers.scope: Direct plate risk; current mill schedules unverified
drivers.analysis: Near-term inventory tightness can sustain price pressure if mills cannot replenish distributors. Raw-steel utilization is broader context. No allocation percentage, shutdown duration or restart is assumed as a confirmed fact.

drivers.name: Imports, Section 232 & trade policy
drivers.scope: Direct plate channel; current shipment treatment unverified
drivers.analysis: The base case holds the reviewed trade framework unchanged as a scenario assumption. Duties, exclusions, antidumping orders and origin rules can alter landed plate competition. All-steel import totals do not prove plate arrivals. Policy easing or a surge in plate-specific licenses would shift this outlook downward; tighter restrictions would shift it upward.

drivers.name: Economy, manufacturing & fabrication
drivers.scope: Broad indicator with a plate demand channel
drivers.analysis: Factory activity and financing conditions influence equipment orders, fabrication backlogs and inventory cycles. Broad manufacturing output supplies only a small model adjustment; it does not measure A36, Grade 50 or pressure-vessel plate orders. A sustained contraction would outweigh the assumed seasonal support.

drivers.name: Energy, oil & gas
drivers.scope: Plate for tanks, vessels and process equipment; indirect cost effects
drivers.analysis: Energy projects can support A516 Grade 70 and structural plate demand, while oil, natural gas, electricity and diesel affect investment and operating costs in different ways. The base case does not translate oil prices one-for-one into plate demand. Project sanctions, drilling budgets, LNG equipment orders and freight costs could change the outcome.

drivers.name: Infrastructure, defense & government policy
drivers.scope: Direct plate applications and broader structural-steel demand
drivers.analysis: Bridges, heavy equipment and eligible defense fabrication can consume plate. Funding announcements become demand only after appropriations, procurement and fabrication orders. Domestic-content rules may shift sourcing. No unverified policy change, election outcome or announced project is counted as a confirmed plate order.

drivers.name: Data centers & power infrastructure
drivers.scope: Mostly indirect; building frames are primarily structural products
drivers.analysis: DOE research supports an electricity-demand growth scenario, not a plate-tonnage estimate. Plate exposure is concentrated in generator skids, tanks, enclosures and selected power equipment. Structural frames, rebar, electrical steel and coil-based products are separate markets. Grid constraints, delayed interconnections or cancelled projects could reduce the expected pull-through.

drivers.name: Historical cycles & seasonality
drivers.scope: Explicit model assumption; not a fitted historical relationship
drivers.analysis: The model allows a year-end inventory and holiday drag, even when supply is constrained. Restocking and destocking can amplify steel cycles. The seasonal weights and mean reversion are judgmental, not a backtested plate-price model. No HRC futures or coil index enters the calculation.

methodology: This is a deterministic, rules-based scenario model. No AI model, paid service, market-data subscription or AI API is running.

Only unexpired, dated primary evidence is eligible. A recognized SSAB plate-price increase contributes +2 directional points; its low distributor inventory assessment contributes +1. Broad manufacturing output adds at most +0.25 or -0.25. Missing inputs contribute nothing; missing plate-price evidence suppresses the directional base case.

For each successive quarter, the initial signal is multiplied by 0.65 to the power of the quarter offset. Judgmental seasonal adjustments are Q1 +0.15, Q2 +0.25, Q3 -0.10 and Q4 -0.50. These are scenario assumptions, not estimated price changes or an empirically calibrated seasonal pattern.

Scores at or above 1.5 mean Firming; 0.5 to below 1.5 Mild upward bias; above -0.5 to below 0.5 Broadly stable; above -1.5 to -0.5 Mild downward bias; at or below -1.5 Softening. The chart maps these labels to ordinal positions -2 to +2. It is not dollars, percentage change, a futures curve or a calibrated probability range.

Bullish and bearish cases shift the base score by plus/minus (1 + 0.2 times quarter offset). These are conditional stress scenarios, not probability-weighted forecasts. Availability normalization is a disclosed assumption, not a dated mill restart forecast.

Trade policy, imports, all-steel output, energy, infrastructure, defense and data centers are disclosed scenario channels, not automatic numerical plate premiums. Raw-steel data cannot confirm plate availability. HRC futures and coil-price indexes are excluded.

The same directional framework covers A36, A572 Grade 50 and A516 Grade 70. Grade, thickness, width, origin, heat treatment and testing requirements can create different availability. A516 Grade 70 pressure-vessel or normalized specifications can be more restrictive; no grade spread or specification premium is estimated.

Each calendar month produces one immutable edition. Explicit revisions append a new edition and reason; prior snapshots remain unchanged. Forecasts are regenerated only with the inputs available at that edition, never backfilled to look historically accurate.

historical_validation.proxy: U.S. steel mill products PPI (not discrete plate)
historical_validation.method: Six- and twelve-month momentum, three-month forward directional evaluation; nonoverlapping quarterly test observations; fixed rules, no optimization; historical revised series may contain revision bias.
historical_validation.warning: This is an all-steel price proxy, not plate prices. Historical accuracy does not establish future probability or forecast confidence.

drivers.name: Energy, oil & gas

drivers.name: Data centers & power infrastructure

methodology: This is a deterministic, rules-based scenario model. No AI model, paid service, market-data subscription or AI API is running.

Plate-first weighted factor model: domestic supply 35%, plate pricing 25%, plate-specific imports and trade 20%, end-user plate demand 15%, and validated historical/macro context 5%. These weights are judgmental and not statistically optimized.
Missing evidence is unscored rather than assumed neutral. Each factor is in [-1,+1] and the sum is scaled to a directional score in [-2,+2]; evidence coverage is reported separately.

Supply tightness is maintained as a conditional base case until verified plate-specific evidence supports recovery. No automatic 35% per-quarter mean reversion or speculative seasonal score is applied. Later-quarter confidence declines even if directional scores persist.

Historical momentum is eligible only if at least 12 nonoverlapping test quarters outperform a naive majority-class baseline by over five percentage points. Its contribution cannot exceed 5% of factor weights.
Bull and bear cases shift scores as illustrative stresses, not measured probabilities. Neither direction nor confidence is a statistically calibrated forecast.

Trade policy, imports, all-steel output, energy, infrastructure, defense and data centers are disclosed scenario channels, not automatic numerical plate premiums. Raw-steel data cannot confirm plate availability. HRC futures and coil-price indexes are excluded.

The same directional framework covers A36, A572 Grade 50 and A516 Grade 70. Grade, thickness, width, origin, heat treatment and testing requirements can create different availability. A516 Grade 70 pressure-vessel or normalized specifications can be more restrictive; no grade spread or specification premium is estimated.

Each calendar month produces one immutable edition. Explicit revisions append a new edition and reason; prior snapshots remain unchanged. Forecasts are regenerated only with the inputs available at that edition, never backfilled to look historically accurate.
